definition: This is a type of will that contains a provision to “pour over” any residual estate assets into a living trust to be overseen by a trustee upon the testator’s death. A testator’s use of a living trust to hold property that remains after the estate is distributed to beneficiaries is useful as it can avoid the probate court process, additional attorney’s fees, and may yield certain federal estate tax benefits. In this way, a well-drafted will that sets up a trust can avoid probate but a poorly drafted one may still pass the estate through probate. Different jurisdictions have adopted their own approaches to pour-over wills. For example, California recently modified its laws to permit trusts to be created after pour-over wills. Such a devise is not invalidated if amended after the will is executed or after the testator’s death.
